compute.body: Semiconductor and electronic-component output grew 19.9%, roughly three times the 6.5% rate for computer and peripheral equipment. Yet semiconductor capacity utilization was 76.5%, below the 81.3% rate for computer equipment. The industry aggregates therefore show much stronger semiconductor production growth without higher overall utilization. Reuters separately reported that Chinese AI firms were rushing to secure Nvidia chip capacity amid concern about U.S. curbs, showing why access to specific advanced chips may differ from broad manufacturing conditions.
compute.headline: Semiconductor output growth far outpaces computer equipment despite lower utilization

data_center.body: Available records list 1,556 data-center sites in development, equal to 0.51 times the 3,068 operating sites; 894 sites are in the tracked active pipeline. Recent reports show individual large projects moving forward: Fluidstack began construction on a 99-acre campus in Virginia, and Fluor won the engineering, procurement and construction contract for a $4 billion Kentucky campus. These projects show activity reaching the construction and contracting stages, but they do not measure the conversion rate of the national pipeline.
data_center.headline: Campus projects move into contracting and construction while 1,556 sites remain in development

economic_impact.body: Nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.1% and real output 2.3%, but real hourly compensation increased only 0.6%. Unit labor costs rose 2.4%. The result is positive growth in output per hour without a comparable gain in workers’ real hourly pay. These aggregate measures do not isolate AI’s contribution, but they provide little evidence that current productivity growth is already translating into broad compensation gains.
economic_impact.headline: Productivity growth continues to outpace real hourly compensation

finance.body: Lender strain rose slightly to 19.6, while borrower strain remains higher at 30.2. Operating cash flow still equals 1.23 times current CapEx, but cash reserves cover only 0.85 years of spending at that rate. Reuters separately reported that Nvidia’s AI-financing activity may persist with less risk appetite. Current spending remains covered by cash generation, but the reserve cushion is limited and some dealmaking may become more selective.
finance.headline: Lender strain edges higher, but borrowers still face more pressure

macro.body: Equity performance has broadened even as the aggregate market signal has softened. The share of covered companies with positive one-year returns rose materially to 63.2%, and the median return reached 10.8%. Yet the AI Equity Index slipped to 35.8 and average sector trading pressure fell materially to 40.9. CoreWeave’s revenue beat and higher guidance eased reported slowdown concerns, but the wider data show improved breadth rather than a uniformly stronger AI trade. Physical expansion remains large, but converting plans into usable capacity is uncertain. Available records show 1,556 data-center sites in development, about half the 3,068 operating sites. Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, faster than the 1.8% increase in total retail demand. Against that demand, the active interconnection queue totals 2,061 GW, yet only 24.2% is in executed-agreement or construction stages, and just 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. Grid operators have filed large-load interconnection reforms at FERC, but the queue remains a measure of proposals and progress rather than delivered supply. Aggregate economic results remain positive but do not identify an AI payoff. Nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.1% and real output 2.3%, while real hourly compensation rose 0.6% and unit labor costs increased 2.4%. Current AI use is reported by 24.6% of businesses, so deployment remains partial. These measures cannot isolate AI’s contribution, and compensation growth remains well below the measured gains in productivity and output.
macro.headline: Equity breadth improves while the power pipeline remains difficult to convert

market.body: The market signal improved in breadth but weakened in intensity. The share of covered companies with positive one-year returns rose materially to 63.2%, and the median return edged up to 10.8%. At the same time, the AI Equity Index slipped to 35.8 and average sector trading pressure fell materially to 40.9. CoreWeave reported revenue above expectations and raised guidance, easing reported concerns about an AI slowdown. The broader readings nevertheless point to wider participation rather than uniformly stronger market conditions.
market.headline: Equity breadth improves as trading pressure falls

power.body: Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, nearly twice the 1.8% increase in total retail demand, while retail electricity prices are up 5.1%. Reuters reported that SpaceX plans a $24 billion gas-power and data-center project in Texas. The proposal is a notable example of generation being planned alongside data-center capacity, but it remains a reported plan and cannot explain the national demand figures. Across the broader pipeline horizon, net planned generation additions total 227.6 GW.
power.headline: A reported $24 billion SpaceX plan combines a data center with gas generation

water.body: The broad county-level drought screen improved materially: 261 campuses, or 17.5% of those with county data, are in counties containing some D2-or-worse drought area. The more concentrated screen moved in the opposite direction. The count in counties where at least one-quarter of the area is D2 or worse rose slightly to 193 campuses, or 13.0%. Fewer campuses are now touched by any qualifying county drought area, but more sit in counties with a substantial affected area. These measures describe county conditions, not campus water use or site-specific availability.
water.headline: Drought exposure narrows overall but becomes more concentrated for some campuses

workforce.body: Only two tracked AI-linked labor channels show positive employment growth, and only two show positive real-earnings growth. Semiconductor manufacturing is the strongest employment channel, with a 2.0% gain, indicating a clear pocket of expansion rather than broad acceleration. Reuters separately reported that Nubank improved its 2026 efficiency-ratio outlook as AI led to slower hiring. It is an example of one firm linking AI to hiring restraint, not evidence of a general employment effect.
workforce.headline: AI-linked labor gains remain concentrated in a few channels

editorial_briefing.style_reference: AI Macro is a research platform that examines the development of the U.S. AI economy from capital investment and physical construction through deployment, adoption, and economic results. It uses publicly available data to relate corporate and market activity to the physical systems required to support the buildout. It evaluates the extent to which that investment produces durable economic value and how its effects are transmitted through the broader U.S. economy.

body.text: The AI Equity Index fell materially to 32.9, and the median one-year return dropped to 9.6%. Breadth also softened: 61.3% of covered companies remain positive over one year, while average sector trading pressure eased to 39.0. CNBC reported that Palo Alto Networks shares surged after an earnings beat, higher guidance and a $4.5 billion AI deal. That company-specific response sits against a broader market signal that has weakened in both breadth and intensity.

headline.text: AI equity momentum weakens despite a company-specific surge

body.text: Borrower strain declined materially to 25.8, while lender strain edged down to 19.2. Borrowers still register more pressure than lenders, but the decline in both measures does not indicate broad deterioration. The Chicago Fed NFCI stands at -0.48, consistent with looser-than-average conditions, although its three-month change of 0.07 points to some recent tightening. Financial conditions therefore remain supportive overall without easing uniformly.

headline.text: Borrower strain recedes while broad financial conditions remain loose

body.text: Computer and peripheral-equipment output growth accelerated materially to 12.0%, while capacity utilization rose to 84.5%. Semiconductor and electronic-component output still grew faster at 15.3%, but growth slowed materially and utilization declined to 74.4%. Computer equipment is now operating at substantially higher utilization even though semiconductors retain faster output growth. Reuters also reported that TSMC tightened China AI-chip curbs as new U.S. rules closed a manufacturing loophole, illustrating how policy can constrain access to advanced chips even when broad semiconductor capacity is not fully utilized.

headline.text: Computer equipment closes the production gap as utilization rises

body.text: Available records list 1,556 sites in development, just over half of the 3,068 operating sites. Investor's Business Daily reported that SpaceX won a permit for a $24 billion Texas data-center project, while Data Center Dynamics reported that Blue Owl's data-center REIT acquired the first building at a Virginia campus. These are concrete project milestones, but they do not establish how quickly the broader development inventory will become operating capacity.

headline.text: Individual projects register permit and acquisition milestones within a large pipeline

body.text: Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, nearly twice the 1.8% rate for total retail demand. Net planned generation additions total 227.6 GW across the pipeline horizon, but future demand assumptions are also under dispute. Utility Dive reported that PJM was urged to delay its base-capacity auction until data-center load was cut from the forecast. The report does not show that the load will disappear; it highlights how estimates of prospective data-center demand can influence capacity planning before projects operate.

headline.text: Data-center forecasts become a point of contention in power planning

body.text: County-level drought exposure increased slightly on both measures. Some D2-or-worse drought area is present in counties containing 264 campuses, or 17.7% of campuses with county data. On the tighter screen, 201 campuses, or 13.5%, are in counties where at least one-quarter of the area is D2 or worse. The move is modest, but the broad and concentrated screens now point in the same direction. These measures describe county conditions, not campus water use or site-specific availability.

headline.text: Drought exposure rises on both county-level screens

body.text: Nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.1% and real output 2.3%. Real hourly compensation rose only 0.6%, while unit labor costs increased 2.4%, so productivity growth continues to outpace growth in workers' real hourly pay. Reuters reported that the Fed's Jefferson said AI was boosting inflation and that a productivity impact may come in the future. The statement supports treating the current aggregate gains as economic context, not evidence that AI has already produced a broad productivity dividend.

headline.text: Aggregate productivity remains firm without resolving AI's contribution
Data-center projects advance as equity momentum cools and power forecasts are contested

paragraphs.text: Financial conditions remain broadly supportive, but equity momentum has weakened. The AI Equity Index fell materially to 32.9, the median one-year return dropped to 9.6% and positive one-year breadth eased to 61.3%. Borrower strain declined to 25.8, lender strain to 19.2 and the Chicago Fed NFCI remained negative at -0.48. The combination is consistent with more selective equity pricing rather than broad financing stress.

Data-center development is moving through project milestones within a large national pipeline. Available records list 1,556 sites in development, about half the 3,068 operating sites, and recent reports include a permit for SpaceX's $24 billion Texas project and Blue Owl's acquisition of the first building at a Virginia campus. Power planning is less settled: commercial demand is growing 3.5%, versus 1.8% overall, and PJM was reportedly urged to delay a capacity auction until data-center load was cut from its forecast. Individual milestones are tangible, but the timing and scale of future electricity demand remain difficult to translate into system plans.

At the aggregate level, the payoff remains unresolved. Nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.1% and real output 2.3%, while real hourly compensation rose just 0.6%; only 24.6% of businesses report current AI use. Reuters reported that the Fed's Jefferson said AI was boosting inflation and that a productivity impact may come in the future. For now, the data show a large buildout and positive economy-wide productivity growth, but not a measured link between them.
